It sounds like you're worried about someone and trying to get him help—that shows real care, even when it's hard.

The Baker Act (in Florida) allows for a temporary involuntary evaluation when someone is a danger to themselves or others, or is severely unable to care for themselves due to mental illness. You generally can't file it yourself, but you can help set it in motion. If there's an immediate emergency or he's in danger, call 911 and tell them your concerns—law enforcement can initiate an evaluation. You can also contact a physician, mental health professional, or a mobile crisis team in your area. Calling or texting 988 (the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline) can connect you with people who can guide you through the right steps for your situation.

If you can share what state you're in, the process may differ, so local crisis resources are your best bet. You don't have to figure this out alone.
